claim_verdicts.evidence: refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt 9.3.4: "The PUT method requests that the state of the target resource be created or replaced with the state defined by the representation enclosed in the request message content."; "If the target resource does not have a current representation and the PUT successfully creates one, then the origin server MUST inform the user agent by sending a 201 (Created) response."; on modifying an existing representation it "MUST send either a 200 (OK) or a 204 (No Content) response". 9.2.2: "PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent."

Not in the local mirror (refs/rfc holds 6265/9110/9111/9112 only; RFC 9110 names PATCH only as a reference to [RFC5789]). WebFetch of rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5789 returned Section 2 verbatim: "In a PUT request, the enclosed entity is considered to be a modified version of the resource ... the client is requesting that the stored version be replaced. With PATCH, however, the enclosed entity contains a set of instructions describing how a resource ... should be modified"; "PATCH is neither safe nor idempotent"; "A PATCH request can be issued in such a way as to be idempotent".

refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt 9.3.5: "If a DELETE method is successfully applied, the origin server SHOULD send" ... "a 204 (No Content) status code if the action has been enacted and no further information is to be supplied, or" ... "a 200 (OK) status code ... includes a representation describing the status" (202 listed first). 9.2.2: "A request method is considered 'idempotent' if the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests with that method is the same as the effect for a single such request. ... PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent."

git -C examples/don-hang grep -nE "HttpPut|HttpDelete|MapPut|MapDelete" stage-1 -- '*.cs' returns no matches. OrdersController at stage-1 declares only [HttpPost], [HttpGet("{id:int}")] and [HttpPatch("{id:int}/cancel")]. Live probe against the running lab (image donhang-api:stage-1; submodule clean at stage-1^{commit} 83c0004): PUT /api/v1/orders/23 -> 405, DELETE /api/v1/orders/23 -> 405, PATCH /api/v1/orders/23/cancel -> 200.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ tag stage-1; live lab on localhost:8080 (2026-09-24)

claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs lines 40-46 are exactly the lesson's block: [Authorize] / [HttpPatch("{id:int}/cancel")] / public async Task<ActionResult<OrderDto>> Cancel(int id) { var order = await orderService.CancelOrderAsync(id); return Ok(ToDto(order)); } — character-for-character, 4-space indent included. The only parameter is the route int id; no body parameter exists. Live: PATCH with no body and no Content-Type -> 200; with no token -> 401; /orders/abc/cancel and /orders/1.5/cancel -> 404.

stage-1 DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs: CancelOrderAsync finds the order (throws KeyNotFoundException when null), sets order.Status = "cancelled", awaits repository.SaveChangesAsync(), then calls notifier.Send(order.Id, "order cancelled") and returns the order. No other Order member is assigned. Live run: customerId, placedAt and items identical in both cancel responses. RFC 9110 9.2.2 allows exactly this: "a server is free to log each request separately ... or implement other non-idempotent side effects for each idempotent request."

Independent live run 2026-09-24 (not the author's session): POST /api/v1/auth/login with anh.tran@example.com / donhang-dev-password returned {"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs..."}; POST /api/v1/orders with productId 2, quantity 1, unitPriceVnd 450000 returned {"id":23,...,"status":"new"}; PATCH /api/v1/orders/23/cancel returned HTTP/1.1 200 OK with "status":"cancelled"; the identical second PATCH returned 200 with an identical body. Every literal value printed in Try it step 1 still matches the lab.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: DELETE requests are stated to carry no body, as an absolute property of the method. RFC 9110 9.3.5 only says "A client SHOULD NOT generate content in a DELETE request unless it is made directly to an origin server that has previously indicated ... that such a request has a purpose and will be adequately supported" — a recommendation with an explicit exception, not a prohibition. Nothing in .meta.json covers it; claim 3 covers only DELETE's 204 and idempotence.
issues.quote: its request carries no body at all, since the URL alone already says which resource to remove
issues.fix: Hedge it the way the rest of the lesson already hedges ("typically answers 204"): "its request normally carries no body, since the URL alone already says which resource to remove". Add a claim to .meta.json (section 4, kind behavior, version_key http, source RFC 9110 9.3.5, "A client SHOULD NOT generate content in a DELETE request"). The mermaid label |nothing| can stay. Quiz q1's explanation c is fine once the prose is hedged.

issues.text: Unlisted claim about ASP.NET Core routing, and looser than the same statement in the already-approved backend.l1.rest-resources: ":int saying only a whole number within the 32-bit range matches". The aspnetcore route-constraint reference gives `int` -> `123456789`, `-123456789`, "Matches any integer", i.e. 32-bit bounded, so an id like 99999999999 does not match either. Not in .meta.json (claim 5 records the attribute text only).
issues.quote: the same `{id:int}` route piece `Get(int id)` uses, which matches only a whole-number id
issues.fix: Either reuse the earlier lesson's wording — "which matches only a whole number within the 32-bit range" — or keep the short form and add it to .meta.json as a syntax claim, version_key aspnetcore, source refs/aspnetcore-docs/aspnetcore/fundamentals/routing.md (route constraint table, `int` row). Verified live: /api/v1/orders/abc/cancel and /orders/1.5/cancel both answer 404.

issues.text: Claim 2 is the only claim with no `version_key`, and its governing document (RFC 5789) is in neither refs/ nor content/versions.yaml: `standards.http` pins RFC 9110, which does not define PATCH (it names [RFC5789] only as a reference). Every PATCH statement in sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 therefore rests on a source the project has not pinned, so the next reviewer cannot re-check it offline as the procedure prefers.
issues.fix: Propose (prompt 08 / owner approval, since versions.yaml is not the lesson skill's to edit) adding `standards.http_patch: docs: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5789` to content/versions.yaml, then set claim 2's `version_key` to `http_patch`. No change to the lesson body: the wording itself is supported by RFC 5789 Section 2.
